audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers ran Skill, Swain, Swain, Skill, Skill, Swain, Swain. The packet chart, the mirror audit and this page's own prose all say Nautilus owns levels 2 through first item.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Skill / Nautilus x5 / Swain and packet.defects flags the contradiction. The nautilus__swain mirror already set both of its layers to exactly that. This page's content layer agrees in words while disagreeing in the chart: whys[1] 'this burst pattern outpaces your fragment-generation', whys[2] 'He controls short all-ins decisively here', whys[3] 'he controls the trade timing', whys[4] his R comes online, content.mid 'Levels 4-5 are the most dangerous stretch'. Only the chart rows said Swain.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-5 flipped to Nautilus in both layers, proposed as one atomic group with the ratings rescaled. Rows 0 (Skill) and 6 (Swain) already matched and were left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The levels 4-5 phase was generic boilerplate about 'the lane-control window' and never named the two abilities that actually own that stretch.
audit.why: Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s shield at every rank that absorbs the opener, and Riptide is three explosions on 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s — a five-second slow zone is what breaks Swain's pattern, not the hook. The page's own content.mid already says the shield eats your first ability; the full layer never mentioned it.
audit.corrected: phases[3].why now names Titan's Wrath and Riptide with their cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Depth Charge is described across the content layer as 'a point-and-click knockup'. Riot's own text describes a shockwave that travels through the earth chasing the target, knocking up enemies it passes under along the way, and erupting on arrival. It is flagged as a projectile, not a point-blank cast.
audit.why: The distinction matters for play: the travel time is why the knockup is telegraphed and why he uses it to start a fight from range rather than as a reactive interrupt. Calling it point-and-click tells the reader there is nothing to see coming.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text rewritten to describe the travelling shockwave and the path knockup. I did NOT restate the 'interrupts Demonic Ascension' claim in the rewritten text — see unverified note.
sources: enemyKit R text and projectile flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Staggering Blow was named nowhere in the full layer despite dontsFull[1] being titled 'Eat his passive root chain', and no real cooldowns appeared in the Do's or Don'ts.
audit.why: Staggering Blow roots on his first attack against a given target, which is what makes any walk-up trade lose. Dredge Line is 1150 range on 14/13/12/11/10s. Nevermove is 850 range on 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s and roots on the RETURN trip — the mirror states the same from Nautilus's side ('Dodge Nevermove twice — the root is on the return — then punish its 10-12s cooldown').
audit.corrected: tldr, phases[1].why, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d now carry the names and numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Dredge Line's terrain behaviour is absent from the page.
audit.why: Colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus toward it, so a wall is a route for him rather than a barrier. Swain has no dash, which makes that mobility the reason a retreat into the jungle is not safe. I did not write the missingInteractions phrasing verbatim ('cut your retreat with Dredge Line') because Riot's text describes him pulling himself to terrain, not creating any.
audit.corrected: Recorded here only — no clean field to place it in without exceeding a length band. Flagged in notes for a future pass.

edits.before: Build MR — W %HP-poke, dodge his hook. Swain wins the Dredge Line cooldown windows.
edits.after: Build MR — poke past Titan's Wrath, then punish Dredge Line's 14-second hook.

edits.before: E-root into the pull is your whole kill setup. Only take the trade when Nautilus's Dredge Line is down.
edits.after: Dredge Line at 1150 range chains into his passive root and Riptide — do not give him a step-up angle.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Dredge Line's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Titan's Wrath eats your opener on a flat 12s and Riptide staggers you at 5-7s — poke on the delay and give nothing else.

edits.before: His only engage. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Dredge Line reaches 1150 and is down 14s at rank 1 — bait it.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Staggering Blow roots on his first auto against you — reset that timer.

edits.before: Burning E on the wave — rootless Swain has no setup, and his all-in just became safe.
edits.after: Nevermove is your only lockdown and is down 12s at rank 1 — hold it for his walk-up.

edits.before: Nautilus's R is a point-and-click knockup that interrupts your Demonic Ascension cast window — stay mobile so he cannot land it into your own tower.
edits.after: Depth Charge tracks you along the ground and knocks up everyone it passes before it erupts — expect the knockup and hold Flash for the follow-up.

notes: UNVERIFIED, left in place deliberately: four fields (content.whys[4], content.mid, content.wants.foe[1], and the original spikes[1].text) assert that Depth Charge 'interrupts' or 'cancels' Demonic Ascension. Swain's R has no channel flag and Riot's text describes an indefinite form sustained by draining, not a channel — so hard CC should not end an active Ascension, though it could interrupt the initial cast. I could not verify which from the kits, so I corrected only the 'point-and-click' mischaracterisation in spikes[1] and left the interrupt claim untouched everywhere. If it is wrong it is repeated in four places and shapes the whole level-6 advice, so it is worth one person checking in a practice tool.
